correctness.rationale: A is symmetric positive-definite integer det1 with charpoly t^3-5t^2+6t-1, distinct positive eigenvalues. The Krylov determinant det(v0,v1,v2)=1 implies e1 has all eigenmode components; any three distinct row vectors v_n=e1^T A^n must be independent, since a nonzero three-term real polynomial cannot vanish at all three positive eigenvalues by Descartes. Haar pushforward then gives independence of the three sampled circle coordinates. For four rows a rank-one primitive integer resonance c yields a four-sign Fourier moment 0 if some c even, otherwise 1/(3 product c), using Poisson smoothing and absolutely summable fourth-order Fourier terms. Consecutive circuit (-1,6,-5,1) is even. Among five 4-subsets only (0,1,2,4) has all-odd circuit (-5,29,-19,1), yielding 1/8265. Sum of five sampling rows is (1,1,1) mod 2, forbidding an all-odd fivefold resonance. Walsh inversion yields the full five-sign law. Independently recomputed all five primitive circuits, all Walsh weights and exact positivity; finite tests do not prove the all-time Descartes or resonance argument.
